result: The authors generated novel MHC class I (B2mtdT) and MHC class II (Cd74tdT) reporter mice using CRISPR/Cas9 to insert P2A-tdTomato constructs at the B2m and Cd74 loci. These reporters enable detection of MHC pathway activation in living mice without disrupting endogenous gene expression or antigen presentation.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly recognized this as 'an important new resource' and 'valuable tools for the analysis of inflammation and neurodegeneration.' While reviewers requested clarification about the 2A peptide mechanism and validation of antigen presentation (essential revisions 20-22), the core finding that functional reporter mice were generated is accepted. The study provides Western blot and functional data supporting intact protein expression.

result: In peripheral immune tissues, B2mtdT was ubiquitously expressed in all immune cells, while Cd74tdT expression was highest in professional antigen presenting cells (dendritic cells, B cells), with tdT levels correlating with MHC class II receptor expression.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these characterization data from spleen. Essential revision 3 asked about the magnitude difference between reporters, indicating acceptance of the data while seeking interpretation. The flow cytometry validation of reporter expression in expected cell types supports the functionality of the system.

result: IFN-γ treatment increased tdT expression in Olig2+ oligodendroglia in cultures from both reporter lines, and also induced expression in microglia and astrocytes in Cd74tdT cultures.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these in vitro validation data. Reviewer 3 requested higher magnification images of the B2mtdT culture data (revision 30), indicating interest in examining the data more closely rather than questioning the finding itself. The IFN-γ induction validates that the reporters respond to inflammatory stimuli.

result: At baseline in adult CNS, Cd74tdT expression was found in meninges, choroid plexus, and some ventral brain microglia, while B2mtdT was expressed in endothelial cells, microglia, and some neurons throughout brain, spinal cord, and retina.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the baseline characterization but requested clarification about specific cell types and anatomical details (revisions 25-29). These requests for additional detail indicate acceptance of the core observations while seeking better documentation. The baseline expression patterns establish the utility of the reporters for detecting constitutive MHC expression.

result: In EAE models, tdT expression increased with disease severity in spinal cord and brain lesions, with both reporters labeling infiltrating myeloid cells and microglia. Co-stimulatory molecule-expressing myeloid cells showed higher tdT expression than non-expressing cells.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these findings as demonstrating the reporters' utility in inflammatory models. Requests for better image resolution and anatomical orientation (revisions 14, 25-27) indicate acceptance of the data while seeking improved presentation. The correlation between reporter expression and disease severity validates the system for tracking inflammation.

result: Olig2+ oligodendroglia expressing tdT were detected in EAE spinal cord lesions, with significantly higher numbers in symptomatic versus pre-symptomatic animals. In B2mtdT mice, tdT+ oligodendroglia were more abundant in lesion areas and correlated with CD45 density and inflammatory activity, though this correlation was weaker in Cd74tdT mice.
evaluation: Reviewers raised concerns about the quantification and statistical significance of these findings. Revision 9 notes 'differences observed are borderline significant and very variable between lesions and non-lesions.' Revision 7 points out discrepancies with published frequencies (0.6% vs 3-4% in Falcao et al.). While the presence of immune oligodendroglia is accepted, the quantitative claims and their interpretation require clarification.

result: Most tdT+ oligodendroglia were mature CC1+ oligodendrocytes rather than PDGFRα+ progenitors, with only a minority (6-17%) being OPCs. The percentage of immune OPCs did not correlate with inflammatory activity, suggesting they are not preferentially depleted.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these findings but requested discussion of the implications (revision 8: 'interesting to discuss why this might be the case'). The data showing predominance of mature oligodendrocytes among immune oligodendroglia is not challenged, though reviewers seek interpretation of why OPCs are less affected.

result: Some Sox9+ astrocytes in EAE lesions expressed MHC reporters, suggesting astrocytes also upregulate MHC in inflammation.
evaluation: Reviewers requested more discussion of astrocyte expression (revision 23: 'Some comment on astrocyte expression... would be of interest'). The observation is accepted but reviewers want it better integrated into the narrative. The finding extends the utility of the reporters beyond oligodendroglia.

result: tdT+ oligodendroglia were also detected in EAE brains and in the AT-CUP model, with numbers increasing with disease severity. Regional analysis showed enrichment in areas of high inflammatory activity, demonstrating the reporters' versatility across inflammatory models.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the brain and AT-CUP data as demonstrating versatility of the system. The regional analysis showing enrichment in inflammatory areas is not challenged. These findings establish that the reporters work in multiple disease models and anatomical regions.

result: Single-cell RNA sequencing of tdT+ and tdT- cells from EAE brains showed that tdT+ cells from Cd74tdT mice were predominantly professional antigen-presenting cells, while B2mtdT tdT+ cells included diverse cell types. Few oligodendroglia were captured in tdT+ samples, suggesting MHC upregulation occurs in a minority or that these cells are destroyed.
evaluation: Reviewers raised significant concerns about the scRNA-seq experiment. Revision 10 notes 'it appears that n=1, and additional biological replicates would be recommended.' Revision 31 questions why brain was used instead of spinal cord and whether stressed oligodendroglia might be underrepresented due to viability issues. While the data are not rejected, reviewers indicate the experiment needs strengthening and better justification.

result: Subclustering of oligodendroglia from Cd74tdT EAE brains revealed eight distinct populations including 'class I' clusters with high MHC I and interferon-responsive transcripts (including PD-L1), 'class II' clusters enriched for MHC II transcripts, and 'stress' clusters expressing cell cycle arrest genes.
evaluation: Reviewers found the oligodendroglia subclustering interesting but raised methodological concerns. Revision 11 asks about further subclustering of cluster 5. Revision 32 requests expansion of the PD-L1 discussion. Revision 33 questions what the heatmap bars represent and requests p-values. The biological interpretation is intriguing but statistical validation and methodological details are needed.

result: Integration with the Falcao et al. 2018 dataset showed high overlap between oligodendroglial subclusters, with differences explained by methodological approaches (OPC reporter vs. no sorting) and tissue source (spinal cord vs. brain), providing evidence of consistent MHC upregulation patterns.
evaluation: Reviewers specifically requested this integration analysis (revision 10: 'integrate their dataset with other similar EAE datasets'). The authors' completion of this analysis and the demonstration of consistency across datasets addresses reviewer concerns and strengthens the findings. The integration validates the immune oligodendroglia populations identified.

result: The study demonstrates that MHC reporter mice enable reliable detection of immune oligodendroglia, which represent a small but diverse population that increases with inflammation and correlates with disease severity.
evaluation: This overarching conclusion is explicitly endorsed by reviewers in the public review: 'compelling demonstration of the new reporter lines as valuable tools' and 'important new resource.' While specific quantitative details were questioned, the core utility and significance of the tool is strongly supported.
